task.name: Unitree Push Recovery
task.objective: Improve a Unitree locomotion policy so it remains upright and recovers stable standing behavior after runner-owned planar x/y pushes.

robot_or_environment.setting: cold-start or warm-start policy trained in the fixed runner protocol

reasoning_guidance: This is a stand-still recovery task: commanded x velocity, y velocity, and yaw rate are zero. There is no forward locomotion command to preserve.

Runner pushes span symmetric world x and y velocity ranges. Do not assume a forward-only or lateral-y-only disturbance; prefer isotropic xy mechanisms unless public evidence supports an axis-specific change.

combine public tensors with bounded arithmetic
set reward weight and optional output clips inside the candidate package
define pure diagnostic callables over prompt-visible RewardInputs
expose bounded public measurements for later feedback
use ScheduleTerm only with allowed effective keys

evidence_discipline: Before authoring, compare the proposed mechanism with public_history.experiment_memory, recent_outcomes, and current-best evidence.
Treat lower scores, failed gates, and dominating or negligible runtime component contributions as negative evidence; do not silently repeat or combine those mechanisms.

Treat last_mean only as the last sampled weighted-contribution snapshot; never infer that a component is inactive or causally ineffective from last_mean alone. Compare max_abs, repeated runtime evidence, and fixed evaluation outcomes.

If reusing a rejected mechanism, the canonical hypothesis narrative embedded in TrainingComponents.rationale must name the closest prior candidate, state the exact code-level difference, and explain how it addresses the observed failure; keep mechanical repair notes out of that hypothesis.
Do not submit numeric-only, string-only, or formatting-only variants of an evaluated source; the historical-source gate rejects those variants before training.
Prefer the accepted current-best source, or when none exists the explicitly nonaccepted best-observed bootstrap anchor.

When an authoring anchor is present, change exactly one named canonical prompt-visible component mechanism relative to it and preserve every other component mechanism; without an anchor, author the complete initial component set.

base_height.name: base_height
base_height.semantics: floating base height above terrain or runner reference plane
base_height.fallback_behavior: zero fallback when root height is unavailable
base_height.candidate_usage_guidance: use as a stance and fall-risk feature with roll and pitch
base_height.known_limitations: zero fallback can make missing observations look like low height

roll.name: roll
roll.semantics: base roll angle derived from root orientation
roll.fallback_behavior: zero fallback when orientation is unavailable
roll.candidate_usage_guidance: penalize large absolute roll as a stability risk
roll.known_limitations: zero fallback can hide missing orientation data

pitch.name: pitch
pitch.semantics: base pitch angle derived from root orientation
pitch.fallback_behavior: zero fallback when orientation is unavailable
pitch.candidate_usage_guidance: penalize large absolute pitch as a forward/backward fall risk
pitch.known_limitations: zero fallback can hide missing orientation data

base_pos_xy.name: base_pos_xy
base_pos_xy.semantics: base xy position relative to the environment origin
base_pos_xy.fallback_behavior: zero vector fallback when base position is unavailable
base_pos_xy.candidate_usage_guidance: use for bounded drift diagnostics, not absolute map location
base_pos_xy.known_limitations: origin-relative position is not a global navigation target

base_lin_vel.name: base_lin_vel
base_lin_vel.semantics: base linear velocity vector as exposed by the runner adapter
base_lin_vel.fallback_behavior: zero vector fallback when velocity is unavailable
base_lin_vel.candidate_usage_guidance: use for recovery damping and excessive drift penalties
base_lin_vel.known_limitations: frame can depend on backend adapter availability

base_ang_vel.name: base_ang_vel
base_ang_vel.semantics: base angular velocity vector as exposed by the runner adapter
base_ang_vel.fallback_behavior: zero vector fallback when angular velocity is unavailable
base_ang_vel.candidate_usage_guidance: use for rotational damping and instability diagnostics
base_ang_vel.known_limitations: frame can depend on backend adapter availability

projected_gravity.name: projected_gravity
projected_gravity.semantics: gravity direction projected into the base frame
projected_gravity.fallback_behavior: zero vector fallback when orientation is unavailable
projected_gravity.known_limitations: zero fallback should not be interpreted as a valid gravity direction

commanded_base_vel.name: commanded_base_vel
commanded_base_vel.semantics: public commanded base velocity vector when a command manager is available
commanded_base_vel.fallback_behavior: zero vector fallback when command is unavailable
commanded_base_vel.candidate_usage_guidance: compare actual velocity to command only when command signal is meaningful
commanded_base_vel.known_limitations: zero command can mean either stand-still command or missing command source

joint_pos.name: joint_pos
joint_pos.semantics: joint position vector in runner joint order
joint_pos.fallback_behavior: zero matrix fallback when joint positions are unavailable
joint_pos.candidate_usage_guidance: use for posture regularization and range diagnostics
joint_pos.known_limitations: joint order is runner-owned and should not be inferred from names

joint_vel.name: joint_vel
joint_vel.semantics: joint velocity vector in runner joint order
joint_vel.fallback_behavior: zero matrix fallback when joint velocities are unavailable
joint_vel.candidate_usage_guidance: use for smoothness and instability penalties
joint_vel.known_limitations: large penalties can suppress recovery actions

joint_pos_error.name: joint_pos_error
joint_pos_error.semantics: joint_pos minus runner default joint position
joint_pos_error.fallback_behavior: zero matrix fallback when default joint position is unavailable
joint_pos_error.candidate_usage_guidance: use for soft posture bias, not hard constraints
joint_pos_error.known_limitations: default posture is runner-owned and task fixed

last_action.name: last_action
last_action.semantics: current policy action vector for the step
last_action.fallback_behavior: zero fallback when action is unavailable
last_action.candidate_usage_guidance: use for action magnitude diagnostics or gentle regularization
last_action.known_limitations: action units are policy-space values, not joint torques

prev_action.name: prev_action
prev_action.semantics: previous policy action vector from runner-owned action history
prev_action.fallback_behavior: zero previous action on first step or reset
prev_action.candidate_usage_guidance: use with action_delta for smoothness diagnostics
prev_action.known_limitations: reset handling can produce legitimate zeros

action_delta.name: action_delta
action_delta.fallback_behavior: current action minus zero on first step or reset
action_delta.candidate_usage_guidance: use to discourage abrupt control changes without blocking recovery
action_delta.known_limitations: over-penalizing action changes can hurt push recovery

push_active.name: push_active
push_active.semantics: per-environment indicator for a push detected on the current runner step; it may come from an explicit public event or the current step-to-step public velocity delta
push_active.fallback_behavior: zero fallback when no push event signal is available
push_active.candidate_usage_guidance: use only as immediate push-onset context; it is not a guaranteed post-push window. Use posture, velocity, and position inputs for continuing recovery
push_active.known_limitations: the indicator is not latched and may be zero on later recovery steps; derived signals can include abrupt public velocity changes when no explicit push event signal is available

push_vec_public.name: push_vec_public
push_vec_public.semantics: current-step public xy velocity delta for a runner-owned push event or observed abrupt base-velocity change
push_vec_public.fallback_behavior: zero vector fallback when no push event signal is available
push_vec_public.candidate_usage_guidance: use to condition immediate response on an already-observed perturbation; use persistent state inputs for subsequent recovery steps
push_vec_public.known_limitations: the vector is not a persistent recovery-window state, is not the runner push distribution, and does not reveal future pushes

progress_fraction.name: progress_fraction
progress_fraction.semantics: runner-owned training progress fraction for the current step
progress_fraction.fallback_behavior: runner supplies a clamped value in [0, 1]
progress_fraction.candidate_usage_guidance: use only for mild annealing inside candidate reward logic
progress_fraction.known_limitations: not an eval metric and not a budget control

selection_guidance: Prefer small code-level RewardTerm changes over parameter-only changes.
Use public feedback to target real failure modes such as falls, drift after push, timeout, or motion-quality gate failures.
If runtime feedback says reward terms did not run or produced zero contribution, fix loading, shape, finite values, or activation first.
Diagnostics are useful public evidence for later rounds but are not sufficient for policy improvement accept.
Treat push_active and push_vec_public as current-step detected perturbation signals, not a guaranteed post-push window; use posture, velocity, and position inputs for continuing recovery.
Do not modify eval protocol, success metric, training budget, seed policy, checkpoint policy, runner code, PPO, or task invariants.
Do not depend on filesystem access, unprojected seed values, non-prompt artifacts, environment objects, optimizer state, or eval internals.

reward_term_runtime_semantics.optimization_direction: Training maximizes total reward: positive weighted contributions reinforce behavior and negative weighted contributions penalize behavior.
reward_term_runtime_semantics.penalty_sign_rule: With a positive weight, a penalty callable must return non-positive values; returning a positive cost rewards the behavior instead of penalizing it.

items.candidate_use: Use the canonical component contract already included in required_candidate_package.component_contract.

Use only as the highest-scoring evaluated bootstrap authoring anchor; it is not an accepted policy best and grants no acceptance authority.
Task provided examples are exposed through known_good_examples when available.
Use the latest nonaccepted source with its verifier, runtime, and eval feedback to repair, refute, or replace the attempted mechanism.
